obligations.obligation: EU AI Act Art. 3(1) AI system definition (scope of the Act)

obligations.artefact: Definitional decision record in the registry: definition applied, elements found, excluded family if any, reason, decider, date

obligations.obligation: GDPR Art. 5(1)(b) and 6(4) purpose limitation

obligations.artefact: Purpose tags on datasets; purpose-match policy in training and indexing pipelines; compatibility assessment record

obligations.obligation: GDPR Art. 6 lawful basis per processing moment
obligations.requirement: A lawful basis for each processing operation, assessed separately for training, fine-tuning, retrieval and inference
obligations.artefact: Basis registry per dataset and stage; versioned legitimate-interest assessment

obligations.obligation: GDPR Art. 7 conditions for consent and its withdrawal
obligations.requirement: Where consent is the basis, the controller can demonstrate it, and withdrawing consent is as easy as giving it
obligations.artefact: Consent-purpose log joined to datasets and model versions; withdrawal propagated to the pipelines

obligations.obligation: GDPR Art. 9 special categories, incl. inferred sensitive data
obligations.requirement: Processing special-category data, incl. biometric data for unique identification, is prohibited unless an Art. 9(2) condition applies, which reaches sensitive data a model infers

obligations.obligation: GDPR Arts. 13–14 transparency to data subjects
obligations.requirement: Inform data subjects of purposes, bases, recipients and retention and, for automated decision-making, give meaningful information about the logic involved (Arts. 13(2)(f), 14(2)(g))
obligations.artefact: Notice generated from the registry entry; model card; automated-decision notice per system

obligations.obligation: GDPR Art. 15(1)(h) access to meaningful information about the logic involved
obligations.requirement: On request, confirm automated decision-making and give meaningful information about the logic involved and its significance and envisaged consequences
obligations.artefact: Per-request explanation generated from the decision record; system-level automated-decision notice

obligations.obligation: GDPR Arts. 15–17 and 21 data subject rights against trained models
obligations.requirement: Access, rectification, erasure and objection requests reach every place the data lives: corpus, snapshots, retrieval index, logs and, where it holds personal data, the model
obligations.artefact: Request workflow across corpus, snapshots, retrieval index, logs and weights; fulfilment record

obligations.obligation: GDPR Art. 22 solely automated decisions and their safeguards
obligations.requirement: A right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing with legal or similarly significant effects, except on contract, law or explicit consent; then human intervention, the right to express a view and to contest (Art. 22(3))
obligations.artefact: Decision record with reason codes; contest channel and human review log; appeal outcomes by group

obligations.obligation: GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) and 25 minimisation and data protection by design and by default
obligations.requirement: Adequate, relevant and limited data, with technical and organisational measures built in at design and set by default
obligations.artefact: Feature justification record; PII and special-category filters; retention as code

obligations.obligation: GDPR Art. 5(2) accountability for a model anonymity claim
obligations.requirement: A controller that claims a trained model holds no personal data must be able to demonstrate it; the EDPB sets an anonymity test and the evidence it expects
obligations.artefact: Anonymity evidence pack; membership-inference and extraction evals in the eval gate

obligations.obligation: GDPR Art. 28 processors, incl. AI vendors
obligations.requirement: Use only processors with sufficient guarantees, under a contract that fixes instructions, sub-processors, security, assistance and deletion
obligations.artefact: AI vendor clause checklist in the due-diligence gate (no training, retention, region, sub-processors, change notice)

obligations.obligation: GDPR Art. 30 records of processing activities
obligations.requirement: Controllers and processors keep a record of the processing activities under their responsibility
obligations.artefact: Records generated per processing moment from the registry and data cards

obligations.obligation: GDPR Arts. 33–34 personal data breach notification

obligations.requirement: Baseline duties for AI operators, heightened duties for "high-impact" AI in sensitive sectors, and AI-content labelling

obligations.appliesNote: In force 2026-01-22; MSIT announced a guidance period of at least one year that holds back fact-finding and fines except in exceptional cases, while the duties apply

obligations.clause: Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI
obligations.obligation: Singapore IMDA Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI (voluntary)
obligations.requirement: Governance dimensions incl. testing, transparency, incident reporting, security and content provenance
obligations.artefact: Eval suite; model cards; content provenance and watermarking

obligations.obligation: UK GDPR Arts. 22A–22D permission-plus-safeguards model for significant, solely automated decisions (Data (Use and Access) Act 2025)
obligations.requirement: A permission-plus-safeguards model for significant, solely automated decisions, with tighter conditions where special-category data is used
obligations.artefact: ADM safeguards: meaningful-human-review path, contest and representation channel, decision notice

obligations.obligation: ETSI EN 304 223 baseline cyber-security for AI models and systems
obligations.requirement: Baseline cyber-security requirements across the AI lifecycle (13 principles over five stages)
obligations.artefact: AI-system security controls across the lifecycle; supply-chain and AIBOM checks; runtime hardening

obligations.clause: Agentic AI framework v1.5: identity and authorisations
obligations.obligation: Singapore IMDA Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI: agent identity and scoped authorisations (voluntary)
obligations.requirement: Each agent has a unique, accounted-for identity, catalogued and centrally managed; authorisations are scoped, time- or session-bound, non-transferable and bounded by the authorising human
obligations.artefact: Agent registry with a workload identity per agent; delegated, short-lived credentials never broader than the user

obligations.clause: Agentic AI framework v1.5: human checkpoints
obligations.obligation: Singapore IMDA Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI: human checkpoints for significant actions (voluntary)
obligations.requirement: Significant checkpoints for high-stakes, irreversible, outlier and user-defined actions, with approvals that are contextual and digestible and enforced through system-level controls
obligations.artefact: Checkpoint classes in the tool gateway; approval log; oversight metrics

obligations.obligation: Canada Directive on Automated Decision-Making (federal institutions)
obligations.requirement: Complete, approve and publish an algorithmic impact assessment before production; apply the Appendix C requirements for the impact level (notice, explanation, peer review, human intervention); offer recourse and report on effectiveness
obligations.artefact: Published AIA rendered from a shared impact fact base; notice and explanation templates; peer-review record; recourse path; re-assessment triggers as code
obligations.appliesNote: In effect since 2019-04-01; modified 2025-06-24; earlier systems complied by 2026-06-24

milestones.note: Current version of the directive
Systems procured before 2025-06-24 meet the updated requirements

obligations.obligation: Brazil LGPD Art. 20 review of automated decisions
obligations.requirement: A data subject may request review of decisions taken solely on automated processing that affect their interests, incl. profiling, and the controller gives clear information on the criteria and procedures used
obligations.artefact: Review workflow; statement of criteria and procedures per system

milestones.note: Administrative sanctions (Arts. 52 to 54) apply

obligations.obligation: Korea AI Basic Act Art. 31(1) prior notice of high-impact or generative AI
obligations.requirement: Tell users in advance that a product or service runs on high-impact or generative AI, in the product, the terms, the screen or the place of supply (Decree Art. 23(1)); a missing notice is finable (Art. 43)
obligations.artefact: Notice component in UI, terms and contracts; notice inventory per user surface
obligations.appliesNote: In force 2026-01-22; MSIT holds back fact-finding and fines for a guidance period of at least one year, while the duty applies

obligations.obligation: Korea AI Basic Act Art. 31(2)–(3) generative-AI output labels and realistic-content notice
obligations.requirement: Indicate that outputs are AI-generated, and notify or label realistic synthetic sound, images or video so users can recognise them; a machine-readable mark alone needs at least one text or voice notice (Decree Art. 23(2)–(3))
obligations.artefact: Provenance pipeline: visible label or machine-readable mark plus at least one text or voice notice
obligations.appliesNote: In force 2026-01-22; MSIT holds back fact-finding and fines for a guidance period of at least one year, while the duty applies

obligations.obligation: Korea AI Basic Act Art. 32 safety duties for high-compute systems
obligations.requirement: Systems with at least 10^26 FLOP of cumulative training compute, built with the most advanced technology and posing broad and serious risk (Decree Art. 24), identify, assess and mitigate risks across the lifecycle and report the results to MSIT
obligations.artefact: Lifecycle risk register; safety-incident monitoring; results report to MSIT
obligations.appliesNote: In force 2026-01-22; MSIT holds back fact-finding and fines for a guidance period of at least one year, while the duty applies

obligations.obligation: Korea AI Basic Act Art. 33 high-impact self-review and confirmation
obligations.requirement: Review in advance whether a system is high-impact AI and optionally ask MSIT to confirm; MSIT replies within 30 days, extendable once (Decree Art. 25)
obligations.artefact: Classification decision record per system: Art. 2(4) area, risk rationale, training-data overview, MSIT reply
obligations.appliesNote: In force 2026-01-22; MSIT holds back fact-finding and fines for a guidance period of at least one year, while the duty applies

obligations.obligation: Korea AI Basic Act Art. 34 measures for high-impact AI
obligations.requirement: A risk management plan, an explanation plan, a user-protection plan, human management and supervision, and documents showing the measures; publish the main content and keep the evidence for five years (Decree Art. 27)
obligations.artefact: Risk management, explanation and user-protection plans; named human overseer; published summary; five-year evidence store
obligations.appliesNote: In force 2026-01-22; MSIT holds back fact-finding and fines for a guidance period of at least one year, while the duty applies

obligations.obligation: Korea AI Basic Act Art. 35 fundamental-rights impact assessment (best effort)
obligations.requirement: Endeavour to assess the effect on fundamental rights before providing high-impact AI, covering the seven elements of Decree Art. 28
obligations.artefact: Impact assessment carrying the seven decree elements
obligations.appliesNote: In force 2026-01-22; MSIT holds back fact-finding and fines for a guidance period of at least one year, while the duty applies

obligations.obligation: Korea AI Basic Act Art. 36 domestic representative
obligations.requirement: An operator with no address or establishment in Korea that meets a decree threshold (revenue, AI-service revenue, daily users or a past fine; Decree Art. 29) designates a domestic representative in writing and reports it to MSIT
obligations.artefact: Designation filed with MSIT; evidence-access runbook for the representative
obligations.scope: Foreign AI business operators above a threshold
obligations.appliesNote: In force 2026-01-22; MSIT holds back fact-finding and fines for a guidance period of at least one year, while the duty applies

obligations.obligation: UK DMCC Act 2024 banned practices: fake and concealed-incentive reviews
obligations.requirement: Unfair commercial practices are prohibited, and Schedule 20 bans submitting or commissioning fake consumer reviews and concealed-incentive reviews, which reaches reviews generated by AI
obligations.artefact: Policy blocking review generation; review-provenance log

obligations.obligation: Provisions on Algorithmic Recommendation (in force 2022-03-01)
obligations.requirement: Algorithm filing for services with public-opinion attributes or social-mobilisation capacity, security assessment, display of the filing number, and a user option to switch off personalised recommendation
obligations.artefact: Algorithm inventory with filing record and number; security-assessment evidence pack; opt-out control at runtime

obligations.obligation: Provisions on Deep Synthesis (in force 2023-01-10)
obligations.requirement: Conspicuous labels where synthetic content could mislead the public and non-removable technical marks; training-data management; separate consent for face and voice editing; filing and security assessment for opinion-shaping functions
obligations.artefact: Content-provenance pipeline (visible label plus metadata mark); training-data governance record; consent gate; pre-release security assessment

obligations.obligation: Interim Measures for Generative AI Services (in force 2023-08-15)
obligations.requirement: Lawful-source training data and foundation models; content labelling under the deep-synthesis rules; security assessment and algorithm filing for opinion-shaping services; stop, remove, retrain and report on illegal content
obligations.artefact: Data-lineage and licensing record; eval gate on generated content; incident pipeline with a retraining loop; filing record
obligations.appliesNote: Binding; in force 2023-08-15; applies to services offered to the public within the PRC

obligations.obligation: Measures for Labelling AI-Generated Synthetic Content with GB 45438-2025 (in force 2025-09-01)
obligations.requirement: Explicit labels (text, audio or graphic) and implicit metadata labels carrying the provider's name or code and a content number; distribution platforms verify metadata and flag suspected AI content
obligations.artefact: Provenance and watermarking pipeline emitting the GB 45438 metadata fields; platform-side detection and flagging
obligations.appliesNote: Binding; in force 2025-09-01, the standard implemented the same day

obligations.obligation: GB/T 45654-2025 Basic security requirements for generative AI services (voluntary; implemented 2025-11-01)
obligations.requirement: Training-corpus source and content screening, model-safety requirements and the evaluation methods that underpin the security assessment
obligations.artefact: Corpus-screening record; eval question banks; security-assessment report

obligations.obligation: TC260 AI Safety Governance Framework 3.0: operators' guidelines §5.3 (voluntary; 2026-09-14)
obligations.requirement: A three-block risk taxonomy (inherent, application, secondary), technological and governance countermeasures and role-based guidelines; operators keep logs for at least six months and audit them, monitor risk in real time, keep a traceable chain of responsibility and assess resilience (§5.3)
obligations.artefact: Risk register keyed to the framework's taxonomy; log-retention policy (six months) with audit; real-time risk monitoring; resilience assessment

obligations.obligation: TC260 Framework 3.0 Appendix 2: agentic AI risk management (voluntary; 2026-09-14)
obligations.requirement: Unique identity and least-privilege permissions per agent by decision mode; human checkpoints with tamper-proof approval logs and deny-by-default; tool and skill verification; runtime guardrails (alert, restrict, intercept, suspend, terminate); memory isolation with no credentials in memory; mutual authentication; sandbox validation, red teaming and re-validation on major change; controlled decommissioning
obligations.artefact: Agent registry with identity and scope; approval-log store; tool allow-list with integrity checks; runtime guardrails and kill switch; memory-scope policy; decommissioning runbook

obligations.obligation: China PIPL Art. 24 automated decision-making and Arts. 55–56 impact assessment
obligations.requirement: Automated decisions stay transparent and fair, with no unreasonable differential treatment in prices or terms; targeted pushes offer a non-personalised option or an easy refusal; individuals may request an explanation and refuse solely automated decisions with a significant impact; an impact assessment beforehand, kept at least three years
obligations.artefact: Explanation service and manual-decision route; non-personalised option at runtime; impact assessment record kept three years

obligations.obligation: Interim Measures for Anthropomorphic Interaction Services (in force 2026-07-15)
obligations.requirement: A minors' mode; AI signals and a reminder after two hours of continuous use; an easy exit; a security assessment at 1 million registered or 100,000 monthly active users; filing
obligations.artefact: Minors'-mode configuration; reminder timer; user-count threshold monitor; security-assessment report; filing record
obligations.scope: Providers of emotional-interaction AI services to the public in China

obligations.obligation: Council of Europe Convention Art. 14(2)(a)–(b) documentation to contest decisions
obligations.requirement: Document relevant information about systems that can significantly affect human rights, sufficient for affected people to contest the decisions
obligations.artefact: Decision record per consequential output; contest path with the record attached
obligations.scope: Parties (states and the EU); private actors through national measures
obligations.appliesNote: Not in force as of 2026-09-24; binds Parties once in force, and the EU implements it through the AI Act

obligations.obligation: Council of Europe Convention Art. 15(2) notice of interaction with an AI system
obligations.requirement: Notify people that they are interacting with an AI system, as appropriate
obligations.artefact: Interaction disclosure enforced at runtime
obligations.scope: Parties (states and the EU); private actors through national measures
obligations.appliesNote: Not in force as of 2026-09-24; binds Parties once in force, and the EU implements it through the AI Act

obligations.obligation: Council of Europe Convention Art. 16 risk and impact management
obligations.requirement: Iterative, graduated risk and impact management: context, severity and probability, stakeholder views, monitoring and documentation
obligations.artefact: Risk register as code; impact assessment linked to the registry; monitoring against a baseline
obligations.scope: Parties (states and the EU); private actors through national measures
obligations.appliesNote: Not in force as of 2026-09-24; binds Parties once in force, and the EU implements it through the AI Act

obligations.obligation: Council of Europe Convention Art. 16(2)(g) testing before first use and on significant modification
obligations.requirement: Test systems before first use and when they are significantly modified, where appropriate
obligations.artefact: Eval gate on release and on material change
obligations.scope: Parties (states and the EU); private actors through national measures
obligations.appliesNote: Not in force as of 2026-09-24; binds Parties once in force, and the EU implements it through the AI Act

obligations.obligation: OECD AI Principle 1.4(b) override, repair or decommission safely
obligations.requirement: Mechanisms let AI systems that risk undue harm be overridden, repaired and/or decommissioned safely
obligations.artefact: Tested kill switch; decommissioning record in the registry
obligations.scope: AI actors (a commitment of adhering governments)

obligations.obligation: OECD AI Principle 1.5(b)–(c) traceability and systematic risk management
obligations.requirement: Traceability of datasets, processes and decisions, and systematic risk management at each phase of the lifecycle
obligations.artefact: Evidence store keyed to registry ids; risk register as code; supplier records
obligations.scope: AI actors (a commitment of adhering governments)

obligations.obligation: G7 Hiroshima Code action 1: lifecycle risk management and pre-deployment testing
obligations.requirement: Identify, evaluate and mitigate risks across the lifecycle, incl. testing before deployment
obligations.artefact: Adversarial red-team suite; eval gate

obligations.obligation: G7 Hiroshima Code actions 2 and 4: post-deployment monitoring and incident sharing
obligations.requirement: Identify and mitigate vulnerabilities, incidents and misuse after deployment, and share information and report incidents responsibly
obligations.artefact: Runtime monitoring; incident pipeline with an external-sharing branch

obligations.obligation: G7 Hiroshima Code action 3: public reporting of capabilities and limitations
obligations.requirement: Publicly report capabilities, limitations and appropriate and inappropriate uses; the OECD reporting framework has collected such reports since 2025
obligations.artefact: Model card published from the registry

obligations.obligation: G7 Hiroshima Code action 7: content authentication and provenance
obligations.requirement: Deploy content authentication and provenance mechanisms where feasible
obligations.artefact: Provenance marking at output; verification test

obligations.obligation: EN 18286:2026 quality management system for EU AI Act purposes
obligations.requirement: Quality-management-system requirements supporting Art. 17; published but not cited in the Official Journal, so it carries no presumption of conformity
obligations.artefact: QMS processes run as pipeline stages; design and change-control evidence
obligations.appliesNote: Published July 2026; not cited in the Official Journal as of 2026-09-24

obligations.obligation: prEN 18228 AI risk management (draft)
obligations.requirement: Draft harmonised standard for the risk management system of Art. 9
obligations.artefact: Provider risk file per system; acceptability criteria as code; control monitoring
obligations.appliesNote: Draft; Enquiry vote closed 2026-07-30, as reported

obligations.obligation: prEN 18229-1 AI trustworthiness framework, Part 1: logging (draft)
obligations.requirement: Draft harmonised standard for the record-keeping of Art. 12
obligations.artefact: Logging specification per system; structured, signed event logs mapped to the draft
obligations.appliesNote: Draft; Enquiry vote closed 2026-08-20, as reported
